evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.34: hoc puerī possunt, virī nōn poterunt?
terms.comment: “Be able to” is a verb in Latin, not an adjective: possum with the infinitive.

terms.gloss: be able; mostly with a negative, “cannot”
evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.1.5: nōn queō reliqua scrībere
Cic. Div. 2.96: cum Dēmosthenēs rhō dīcere nequīret (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero himself writes nōn queō in the first person singular (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: be strong enough to, have the power to
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation; with an infinitive mostly in poetry and post-Augustan prose
evidence: Hor. C. 1.34.12–13: valet īma summīs mūtāre … deus (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: hoc puerī possunt, virī nōn poterunt?
phrases.english: children are able to do this, and men won’t be?

phrases.latin: caprās et ovēs quot quisque habēret, dīcere posse, amīcōs quot habēret, nōn posse dīcere
phrases.english: anyone can say how many goats and sheep he has, but not how many friends

phrases.latin: nōn queō reliqua scrībere; tanta vīs lacrimārum est
phrases.english: I can’t write the rest; the tears are too many
